title: A Software Platform to Support Disaggregated Quantum Accelerators
problem: Quantum computers integrated into HPC centers form disaggregated infrastructures with diverse implementations and significantly fewer units than compute nodes, requiring sophisticated resource management strategies for efficient utilization as shared resources.
motivation: Integrating quantum accelerators into HPC environments enables practical hybrid quantum-HPC computing for scientific research while optimizing resource utilization.
method: MQSS uses a compile-at-runtime (JIT) optimization stack that works across any quantum hardware type (hardware-agnostic). When quantum circuits are too large for a single device, it splits them into smaller parts using quantum circuit cutting. It then dynamically selects which available quantum accelerator should handle each workload through a unified Quantum Device Management Interface (QDMI).
key_novelty: MQSS introduces a unified Quantum Device Management Interface that dynamically routes hybrid computing workloads (mixing classical and quantum tasks) to the best available quantum accelerator, enabling multiple different quantum computers to function as a shared resource.
contributions: JIT compilation and execution stack for hybrid HPC-quantum workloads
Hardware platform selection process for disaggregated quantum resource allocation
Quantum Device Management Interface (QDMI) providing unified access to heterogeneous quantum accelerators
Hardware-agnostic optimization and quantum circuit cutting techniques
primary_theme: Quantum accelerator integration and resource management for HPC
